sources.title: Prescription Medications to Treat Overweight and Obesity
Food and nutrition when taking weight-loss medicines
sources.organization: Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust

sources.title: Managing side effects with diet
sources.organization: Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust

questions.text: A family WhatsApp group recommends a GLP-1 medicine. Is that enough to decide it is safe for you?
options: Yes, if someone I trust uses it
No, I need an individual medical review
questions.explanation: Someone else’s experience cannot establish your safety. A clinician needs to review your history, medicines and possible benefits and risks.

questions.text: Your usual lunch is roti and sabzi. Which addition can help include protein?
options: Dal, chana, curd or another suitable protein food
Skipping lunch altogether
questions.explanation: Protein foods can help support muscle during weight loss. Pulses and dairy are options; your dietitian can adapt choices to your needs. Food alone cannot guarantee muscle preservation.

questions.text: Myth or fact: eating less is all you need to think about to protect muscle during weight loss.
options: Fact
Myth
questions.explanation: Myth. Nutrition and strength-building activity both matter. Ask your care team about suitable protein foods and resistance exercise, adapted to your abilities.

questions.text: Which can occur with GLP-1 weight-management medicines?
options: Nausea or constipation
No digestive side effects at all
questions.explanation: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation can occur. These medicines slow food moving through the gut. Discuss symptoms with your care team.

questions.text: A friend taking a weight-management medicine cannot keep fluids down. What is the safer response?
options: Ignore it because all side effects are harmless
Seek prompt medical help
questions.explanation: Being unable to keep fluids down can lead to dehydration and needs medical attention. Do not dismiss persistent or worsening symptoms as a normal part of treatment.

questions.text: Myth or fact: everyone gets exactly the same side effects from a weight-management medicine.
options: Myth
Fact
questions.explanation: Myth. Side effects differ between medicines and people. An individual discussion of risks and follow-up is important; a quiz cannot predict your experience.

questions.text: Your work commute is difficult because of persistent nausea on treatment. What next?
options: Copy a dose change suggested online
Contact the prescribing team for advice
questions.explanation: Follow your prescription instructions and ask your doctor or pharmacist about problems. Do not copy another person’s dosing schedule.

questions.text: Myth or fact: stopping a weight-management medicine guarantees the weight stays off.
options: Fact
Myth
questions.explanation: Myth. Weight regain can happen after stopping treatment. Discuss a long-term plan with your clinician; neither medicine nor habits offer a permanent-results guarantee.

questions.text: Myth or fact: GLP-1 medicines are only ever used for diabetes.
options: Myth
Fact
questions.explanation: Myth. Some GLP-1 medicines are used for weight management as well as diabetes. Uses differ by product and local approval; this does not mean everyone is eligible.

questions.text: A colleague says a GLP-1 medicine worked for them. Does that mean it suits you?
options: Yes, colleagues can use the same plan
No, suitability needs an individual assessment
questions.explanation: Treatment suitability depends on your health and circumstances. A qualified clinician, not a friend’s result, should assess whether prescription treatment is appropriate.

questions.text: What can this three-question quiz tell you?
options: What you learned—not whether you qualify for medicine
Which medicine you should start
questions.explanation: This is an educational quiz, not a clinical assessment. Prescription decisions require a qualified clinician and an individual discussion.

questions.text: A cousin offers their prescribed GLP-1 medicine so you can try it. What should you do?
options: Try it before booking a consultation
Do not use someone else’s prescription; seek your own medical advice
questions.explanation: These are prescription medicines. Use only treatment prescribed for you, following your own clinician’s instructions.
